source_snapshot.criteria: Blue On, Blue 1 Hz blink, Off for the three commands.

old_problem: Prior review called all raw bytes platform-specific and left them pending. In fact netfn 0x00/cmd 0x04 is standard IPMI Chassis Identify; only the implementation's physical Blue/steady/1 Hz behavior, indicator map and tolerances are project bindings.
disposition_reason: Intel IPMI 2.0 section 28.5 defines interval 00h as Identify Off, byte-2 bit0 as Force Identify On indefinitely, and interval 0x0f as 15 seconds (-0/+20%). The source itself supplies Blue and 1 Hz expectations. Thus command semantics are authoritative; board indicator mapping/tolerances and real visual evidence remain runtime gates under ED-03/09.
decision_basis: Direct XLSX rows 2263 and 2264, same-row AI fields, GPT V2, historical record, unique identity and ED-01 through ED-30 were reviewed.

Intel IPMI 2.0 Table 28-6 defines Chassis Identify command 0x04: `00h` interval turns Identify off; optional force bit 1 overrides interval and turns it on indefinitely; `0x0f,0` drives a 15-second timed identify.
IPMI deliberately leaves physical identify mechanism to the implementation, so Blue steady versus 1 Hz blink must be proven on the mapped LED by timestamped video.
Issue the three literal raw commands once in order with completion codes/readback and restore Off even after intermediate failure.
Do not silently substitute Redfish or `chassis identify`; an alternate is supplemental unless byte-for-byte/state equivalence is documented.
No IPMI command, UID state change, visual observation, retry or DUT action occurred.

test_case.test_name: Standard IPMI UID Blue On, timed 1 Hz blink and Off
test_case.purpose: Exercise the standard Chassis Identify force-on, 15-second timed-identify and off encodings while visually proving the intended UID indicator's Blue steady/1 Hz/off states and guaranteed final Off.
required_package: Bound SUT/BMC/board and UID front/rear indicator map
IPMI transport/credentials and Force Identify support
Blue color plus steady/1 Hz frequency/duty/settle/observation tolerances
Qualified visual observer/video and approved final Off recovery
test_case.test_command: After target/observer approval, record initial state; run once in order: `ipmitool raw 0x00 0x04 0 0x01`, `ipmitool raw 0x00 0x04 0x0f 0`, and `ipmitool raw 0x00 0x04 0 0`; capture completion/timestamps/readback and SUT-linked video, then independently verify final Off.
test_case.expected_result: Force-on command produces the source-required Blue steady On state; timed command produces Blue 1 Hz identify for the required observation/15-second interval; Off command extinguishes the mapped indicator; all commands complete once and final readback/visual state is Off.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires literal command evidence plus real physical Blue/steady/1 Hz/Off video within signed tolerances and final Off. Completion code or software state alone cannot pass. Unsupported force byte, wrong LED/color/cadence, early/late timed state or failed Off is FAIL/BLOCKED as applicable.
safety_gate: Verify exact BMC/UID mapping and one-shot order.
Qualified safe physical observation; no inference from readback alone.
Final Off is mandatory after any intermediate error.
No blind retry or unapproved API substitution.
expected_evidence: Video proving Blue steady and measured 1 Hz timed state
test_case.recovery: If any intermediate command or visual state fails, do not repeat it; issue only the pre-approved Off restoration once if safe, verify physical Off, preserve evidence and escalate.
